statement: Regular dodecagon $ABCDEFGHILMN$; $P$ = intersection of diagonals $AF$ and $DH$; $S$ = circle through $A,H$ with same radius as circumcircle but different. Prove: (1) $P$ lies on $S$; (2) center of $S$ lies on diagonal $HN$; (3) $PE$ equals the side length of the dodecagon.
An $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ square is divided into $(n-1)^2$ unit squares. Color each of the $n^2$ vertices red or blue so each unit square has exactly 2 red vertices. Find the number of such colorings.
Find all $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying: (i) $f(m)<f(n)$ whenever $m<n$; (ii) for each pair $(m,n)$, there is an integer $k$ with $f(m)-f(n)=f(k)$.
Find all triples $(a,b,c)$ of positive integers with $a^2 + 2^{b+1} = 3^c$.

Acute $\triangle ABC$ with all angles in $(45^\circ, 90^\circ)$. (a) Prove three equal squares can be placed inside $\triangle ABC$ with a common interior vertex $K$, each touching two sides of $\triangle ABC$. (b) Let $P$ be the center of the square with side $AB$ outside $\triangle ABC$; $r_C$ = line symmetric to $CK$ w.r.t. bisector of $\angle BCA$. Prove $P$ lies on $r_C$.

Francesca and Giorgia play with stacks of coins. A move: split an even-size stack into two equal halves, or remove all odd-size stacks. First to remove the last coin wins. (1) Starting with $2008^{2008}$ coins in one stack, who wins? (2) Characterize all initial configurations where Francesca wins.
